papers.title: The space of equators has infinite Hofer's diameter
papers.abstract: We settle several questions about Hofer's geometry of the two-sphere. We prove that the space of equators has infinite Hofer diameter, construct simple commutators of arbitrarily large Hofer norm, and exhibit a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism whose iterates escape to infinity in Hofer distance from the set of autonomous diffeomorphisms. Finally, we construct a bi-Lipschitz group monomorphism from the free group of rank two, equipped with its conjugation-invariant generator norm, into the Hamiltonian group equipped with Hofer's metric. The proof rests on an interplay between Lagrangian Floer theory in the fourth symmetric product of the sphere and combinatorial group theory. This paper was written with substantial assistance from AI.

papers.title: The Pu inequality and the Viterbo conjecture with finite symmetry
papers.abstract: We study a construction for producing Finsler metrics on the sphere from convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^4$ using the quaternions. Among several applications, we prove the weak Viterbo conjecture for convex bodies in $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are invariant under the natural action of the quaternion group $Q$. This is the first instance where Viterbo's systolic inequality is established for convex bodies with a finite group symmetry, addressing a question of Haim-Kislev-Ostrover. Moreover, a smooth $Q$-symmetric convex domain that achieves equality is symplectomorphic to the ball, without any assumption of strict or uniform convexity. Finally, we show that any link of minimal Reeb orbits on the boundary of a uniformly convex $Q$-symmetric convex body is transversely isotopic to a union of Hopf fibers, strengthening a result of Abbondandolo-Edtmair-Kang in the $Q$-symmetric setting.

papers.title: Weinstein Handlebodies for the Painlev\'e Betti Spaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the generic fibre of the Betti moduli space associated to any of the ten Painlev\'e equations coincides with the result of attaching Weinstein handles along the Stokes Legendrian, and provide Weinstein handlebody diagrams for each of them in the process. We moreover extend the procedure for obtaining presentations in Gompf normal form of Weinstein manifolds obtained by attaching handles to Legendrian lifts of cooriented curves in surfaces to their unit cotangent bundle to the case where the surface may have nonempty boundary.

papers.title: The contrast between real and $p$-adic integrability
papers.abstract: A fundamental question in $p$-adic symplectic geometry and $p$-adic Hamiltonian mechanics is to what extent we can learn new information about integrable systems with coefficients in the rational numbers $\mathbb{Q}$, if we view them as $p$-adic systems instead of real ones. We combine geometric analytic estimates with Galois theory in order to show that at a local level, these real and $p$-adic viewpoints give completely different information. Then we focus on understanding this local behavior for the $p$-adic case by proving effective methods to compute local normal forms. Our results are motivated by a program outlined by Pelayo-Voevodsky-Warren a decade ago, to develop a $p$-adic theory of integrable systems and symplectic geometry.

papers.title: Cluster structures from Legendrian double twist knots: a comparative approach
papers.abstract: We undertake a systematic comparison of cluster algebras associated to Legendrian knots of the same smooth knot type. We describe a cluster structure on the m-graded augmentation variety of Legendrian representatives of a family of double twist knots that includes all orientably Lagrangian fillable twist knots. For different Legendrian representatives of the same smooth knot type, we show that these cluster structures are equivalent. Along the way, we characterize the representatives that admit Maslov-m exact Lagrangian fillings, construct a Catalan number of such fillings for each representative, and show that any Maslov-0 fillable representative is Legendrian isotopic to the (-1)-framed closure of a positive braid. Finally, we give two Legendrian representatives of a cabled twist knot that yield equivalent cluster structures of infinite type.

papers.title: A Smooth Hamiltonian Diffeomorphism with Two Fixed Points on $S^2\times S^2$
papers.abstract: We give a construction of a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of the equal-area symplectic product $S^2\times S^2$ with two fixed points. The argument starts with a four-fixed-point map, passes to rescaled cotangent coordinates near the antidiagonal, and reduces the local fixed-point equations to two planar saddle problems. A relative modification merges each pair of saddles, and mixed generating functions are used to transfer the modification to the original map. We include detailed explanations of the normal form along a level arc, the Moser equation, uniform existence of mixed generating functions, the order of parameter choices, and the global graph argument. This construction gives a counterexample to the degenerate version of Arnold's conjecture proposed by Arnold\cite{Arnold86} when the manifold is standard $S^2\times S^2$. This work is done with ChatGPT. The author gave the idea to study the limit behavior of $\Phi_\rho$. GPT suggested a key idea of using second generating function to construct this Hamiltonian. Also, most of the computation is done by GPT.
